No public UBO register exists; ownership information is filed at the commercial registry but beneficial-owner data is held only for government and

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as last amended, Book II, Chapter on Companies, Articles 287 through 287-44 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), together with Articles 288 (formation by articles of association), 289 (contents of articles of association), 290 (contributions of members), and 294 (registration of incorporation); Supreme Court Regulations on Corporation Registration; Electronic Commerce Consumer Protection Act for online mail-order seller notification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office (Deung-gi-guk) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; the Supreme Court of Korea maintains the centralized company registration data system and the i-register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, filed on the court-prescribed form, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Association and all statutory annexes required by the Commercial Act and Supreme Court registration regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean commercial law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Association must state the total aggregate contribution and each member's contribution. All contributions must be fully performed before the incorporation registration; for cash contributions, a bank certificate of deposit or

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); electronic administration portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity such as Yuhan Hoesa (KR_YUHANGHOESA) that will make taxable supplies in Korea, the entity must first determine whether it has a domestic place of business. If no domestic fixed place exists, it must appoint a Korean tax representative and file a non-resident business registration application with the National Tax Service, either in person at the competent district tax office or online through the HomeTax portal using the non-resident electronic registration menu. The filing must include the entity's certificate of incorporation or equivalent constitutional document, corporate register extract or articles of association, evidence of its foreign tax identification number or official business registration in the home jurisdiction, a power of attorney appointing the Korean tax representative, and proof of the representative's Korean address. NTS will process the application and issue a 10-digit Korean Tax Identification Number (Business Registration Number, which also serves as the VAT registration number) and a Business Registration Certificate. Registration must be completed within 20 days of the commencement of taxable business activities in Korea. Foreign suppliers of electronic services may use the simplified non-resident registration facility in HomeTax but a Korean tax representative is still required for service of documents and compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box or any elective pass-through classification for a Yuhan Hoesa. The entity is statutorily classified as a Korean domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily under Korean international tax law and cannot be elected out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold: every person making taxable supplies in Korea is required to register for VAT irrespective of turnover, under the Value-Added Tax Act. Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services are required to complete simplified VAT registration from the first taxable supply made to Korean customers. Applicable threshold in KRW: N/A (mandatory registration from business commencement).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices issued between registered businesses must be issued as electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) through the National Tax Service HomeTax system or a certified e-invoice service provider. The e-invoice must be transmitted to NTS no later than the day following its issuance. There is no separate real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping; Korea instead relies on mandatory e-invoice API transmission and the NTS automatic cross-checking system for transaction-level matching. For retail sales not covered by a tax invoice, a Cash Receipt must be issued and reported to NTS. Export sales must be recorded with zero-rated e-invoices or export electronic tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported goods as well as foreign-currency-earning services under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act. For the online sale of musical instruments and studio audio gear, zero-rating applies to physical goods supplied to a foreign buyer where the goods are actually exported from Korea under a customs export declaration, ownership passes to the foreign buyer, payment is received in foreign currency or an approved settlement method, and the export proceeds are repatriated within the statutory deadline. For digital or electronic services, zero-rating is restricted to services performed and consumed outside Korea; digital services supplied to Korean consumers are taxable at the standard 10% rate under the place-of-supply rules. The exporter must maintain an auditable file containing export contracts, shipping documents, customs export declarations, invoices, and bank settlement records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (export clearance certificate or reference number with item description and FOB value)
Signed commercial invoice and foreign buyer purchase order or export contract
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods out of Korea
Certificate of Acquisition of Foreign Exchange (foreign exchange settlement certificate) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt and repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the National Tax Service determines that a zero-rated export claim lacks actual export, a valid customs declaration, or timely foreign exchange repatriation, it will deny the zero-rating and assess VAT at the standard 10% rate on the full supply value. The assessment is subject to statutory interest and penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including a 10% penalty for erroneous underreporting and up to 40% for fraudulent understatement. Any input VAT deducted in relation to the failed export is retrospectively clawed back, and additional penalties apply for false e-Tax Invoices or non-issuance of tax invoices. Korea Customs Service may also impose customs penalties or refer the matter for criminal prosecution for export fraud. The NTS may open retrospective audits within the statutory assessment periods, which are extended for cross-border or fraudulent cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but administratively monitored foreign exchange system. Current-account transactions are freely convertible and South Korea has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, meaning trade-related receipts and payments are generally unrestricted. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment into a Yuhan Hoesa, are also encouraged, but they must be reported through a registered foreign-exchange bank and, where applicable, registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no general restriction on holding foreign currency, and a Korean limited-liability entity may maintain foreign-currency deposit accounts alongside KRW accounts. Profit remittance hurdles are largely procedural rather than impeditive: a foreign shareholder can remit dividends provided the company has completed external taxation, filed the appropriate withholding report, and the bank verifies the board dividend resolution and audited financial statements. Surrender requirements have been significantly liberalised; export receipts are not forcibly converted into KRW, but the receiving bank must be informed, and any conversion is executed at the market rate. Overall, Korea's regime is best described as free convertibility with reporting-based controls rather than approval-based controls for ordinary trade, while certain capital flows above reporting thresholds require a foreign-exchange transaction form and supporting documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related regulations, South Korea does not impose mandatory conversion ratios or an obligatory surrender of export foreign-currency receipts. Exporters are required to settle export proceeds through domestic foreign-exchange banks within the agreed contractual maturity, which for open-account or deferred-payment exports is generally no more than one year from the date of shipment unless an extension is approved by the relevant bank. Receipts may be retained 100% in foreign-currency deposit accounts or freely converted into Korean won at market rates. If retained, subsequent cross-border outbound use must comply with transaction reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD multi-currency) plus Capital Escrow Account for foreign direct investment proceeds
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account with E-Trade processing
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Term Deposit for export proceeds
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account for inbound FDI and outbound import settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for regulatory account-opening and onboarding of the Korean entity. South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires foreign-exchange business to be conducted by registered foreign-exchange banks, and offshore digital EMIs do not hold Korean banking licences and cannot issue KRW-denominated operational accounts or execute FX settlement for a domestic LLC. Stripe and PayPal are acceptable as payment-collection sub-merchant rails for online sales of musical instruments and studio audio gear, but treasury clearing and capital movement must be anchored in a licensed Korean bank account. Any attempt by the Yuhan Hoesa to use an offshore EMI as its primary transaction account would create unlicensed foreign-exchange brokerage risk, invite AML scrutiny by the Financial Supervisory Service, and materially delay or block outbound trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is the baseline requirement for corporate account opening in Korea. At least one statutory director or the legal representative of the Yuhan Hoesa must appear in person at a Korean bank branch with the corporate seal certificate, certificate of corporation registration, and business registration certificate. Remote opening may be accepted only where the bank has an existing customer relationship and a video-recorded e-Sign process, but consular proxy opening by a non-representative third party is generally not permitted. Foreign directors may complete identity verification at a branch with passport, alien registration card, and notarised power of attorney, although most compliance officers will still require a video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or non-transparent ultimate beneficial ownership of the Korean LLC, especially where foreign shareholders hold through a chain of shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registration, chronological shareholding registry, UBO declaration, passport copies and residency proof of all natural-person UBOs, legal-person shareholders' business licences, and a management and ownership chain chart signed by the authorised director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border injection of initial capital without verifiable source of wealth, triggering suspicion of unregistered foreign direct investment or money laundering under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and FSS AML guidelines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-verified trail of the overseas remitter, 12 months of personal or corporate bank statements showing the origin of funds, executed sale or service contracts for the musical-instrument and audio business, tax return of the funding shareholder, a signed declaration of source of funds, and submission of the Foreign Investment Report Certificate to the receiving bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained involvement of third-country beneficiaries in export payments or mismatches between the ISIC 4791 product line and contract descriptions creating trade-based money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial invoices with HS codes for musical instruments and studio audio gear, packing lists, bill of lading, customs entries, proof of actual dispatch, counterparty sanctions screening report, and a written beneficial-owner confirmation from each overseas buyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on non-resident authorised signatories with unrestricted powers, increasing risk of unauthorised disbursement or control fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board resolution defining signing limits and dual-control approval, apostilled power of attorney, passport and ARC copies of each signatory, specimen signatures, fraud and AML training acknowledgement, and a recorded video interview with each signatory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment must be reported at the receiving foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before issuance of a Foreign Investment Report Certificate. The remitter must wire funds via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code for foreign direct investment in a Korean corporation to the Capital Escrow Account held in the Korean LLC's name at a registered foreign-exchange bank. The bank performs capital verification by matching the certificate value, the share subscription agreement, and the actual credit advice. Once verified, funds may be converted into KRW at market rate and transferred to the company's Basic Operational Currency Account. All inward remittances must be properly reported through the receiving bank, and the standard foreign-exchange transaction form must reflect the true nature of the equity capital.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for standard supplier payments and commission disbursements, with the correct trade purpose code entered on the foreign-exchange transaction form. For high-value procurement of musical instruments and studio audio gear, an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit provides stronger protection, while Documentary Collections are suitable for established supplier relationships where baseline settlement is acceptable. All outbound FX payments must be covered by an underlying transaction, and payment files should be reconciled against purchase orders and import customs declarations to satisfy the bank's trade-based AML review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with attached financial statements and 10 percent local corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax and the competent local government via WeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20 percent unfaithful-return additional tax if no return is filed and 10 percent if materially under-declared; daily overdue interest of 0.022 percent on unpaid tax until paid; prolonged delinquency permits NTS asset seizure and administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' general meeting approving the balance sheet, income statement, profit-appropriation or loss-processing and, if applicable, appointment of external auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate body; signed minutes and annexed financial documents retained at the registered office and produced to NTS or the court on demand; not a registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fixed administrative fine for late internal approval standing alone, but failure to hold a demanded meeting or to keep statutory minutes exposes officers to non-criminal fines up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act and defects the external-audit trail.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified audit report (statutory external audit) where the Yuhan Hoesa meets the mandatory audit threshold or is otherwise required by a supervisory statute
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (attached to the annual corporate tax return); Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the report attached to the annual corporate tax return due by March 31 for a calendar fiscal year; where FSS disclosure applies, within 20 days after the annual meeting or as specified under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to submit the audit report triggers penalties under the External Audit Act, including officer fines up to KRW 30 million; NTS may also treat the income tax return as defective and reassess tax plus daily overdue interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT preliminary return for January - March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax; electronic tax invoice approval obligations apply)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 following the January - March period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing additional tax under the VAT Act at 0.5 percent per day of unpaid VAT for early delay, escalating daily surcharge thereafter; chronic non-filing allows NTS estimated assessment, seizure and administrative closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT final return for January - June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax under the VAT Act for late or deficient filing plus 0.022 percent daily overdue interest on unpaid VAT; sustained delinquency permits NTS tax-collection seizure and business-registration closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT preliminary return for July - September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 following the July - September period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing additional tax as prescribed by the VAT Act at 0.5 percent per day for early delay, plus daily overdue interest; repeated non-filing triggers NTS estimated assessment and administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT final return for July - December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT late-filing additional tax plus daily 0.022 percent overdue interest on unpaid tax; unpaid or unfiled year-end VAT is a legal basis for NTS seizure and administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven commercial registry amendment (registered office, directors, statutory representative, capital, articles) and NTS business-registration change notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Court Commercial Registry and local tax office / NTS HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the triggering event; not a fixed annual date; beneficial-ownership changes that alter the statutory representative or registered office are included
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register without just cause carries administrative fines under the Commercial Act, generally up to KRW 5 million; unregistered matters may not be asserted against bona fide third parties, and NTS may impose separate business-registration change penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit applies if: (1) total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million at 1,330 KRW/USD); (2) the company is listed or subject to public disclosure under the Capital Markets Act; (3) the company is a financial institution, insurance company, securities company, mutual savings bank, or other entity under a special supervisory statute; (4) the company is required by Presidential Decree or FSS order to file audited financial statements; or (5) NTS or another competent authority orders an audit. A small private Yuhan Hoesa below these thresholds is exempt from the mandatory external audit but must still maintain books and accounts and may adopt a voluntary review or audit for financing or due diligence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed and statutorily designated enterprises; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP / General Corporate Accounting Standards) for non-public companies below the K-IFRS mandate; tax-basis accounts prepared under the Corporate Tax Act and the Basic Act for National Taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea has no separate annual UBO certificate filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa. The company must maintain and update a current Register of Members upon every transfer of equity; obtain a members' resolution before admitting a transferee who is not already a member unless the articles permit otherwise; reflect any resulting change of director or statutory representative in the Commercial Registry and NTS business registration within 30 days of the event; report qualifying foreign-investment changes to the competent ministry or KOTRA within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and retain and provide beneficial-owner identification to Korean banks and financial institutions on demand under AML/CFT customer due diligence rules set out in the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information. There is no government renewal confirmation of beneficial ownership annually except for regulated-industry regimes.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,800 per year for a registered or virtual office and service address in Seoul or Busan used by an online retailer; virtual office for a nonresident-owned LLC is a standard arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,000 for a voluntary or review engagement of a small online retailer; USD 8,000 - 25,000 for a statutory audit when the KRW 12 billion asset threshold or regulated-industry test is met

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for ISIC 4791 online retail. SMEs may benefit from reduced effective rates through the small-company rate grace (max bracket lowered to 20% for taxable income up to 200 billion KRW).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Tax Bases and Tax Calculation Statement, Form 1) filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic system (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 FYE), subject to filing extension for approved situations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and calculation period (year-end date).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact year-end date of the Korean entity; for a non-resident-owned Korean LLC the calendar year is standard, but can be any 12-month period.
Report gross revenue from all Korean operations, including online sales of musical instruments and audio gear; clearly separate domestic and export sales.
Only exclude income exempt under the Corporate Tax Act or tax treaties; do not treat foreign-source income as exempt unless supported by the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (cost of sales, SG&A, intercompany charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide invoices, contracts, and TP documentation when deducting costs from foreign related parties; arm's-length pricing must be verifiable.
Apply loss carryforward if available; the resulting positive amount is subject to corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax computation at progressive rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 10/20/22/25% brackets accurately; for foreign investment enterprise, any treaty-based tax credit needs to be separated.
Include foreign tax credits or early payments made at period-end; attach schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax due after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure any remaining balance is paid by the statutory deadline to avoid penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file timely: additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax. Underreporting: 10% additional tax. Fraudulent underreporting: 20%. Daily overdue interest on unpaid amounts: 0.022% per day.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% plus 2% local resident surtax (aggregate 22%) when no treaty applies
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced withholding, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit Form for Application for Reduction/Exemption of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty (Form 20-2) together with the Certificate of Tax Residence issued by its home tax authority, to the Korean payer before payment. The payer then withholds at the treaty rate. If over-withheld, a refund must be sought through the competent authority procedure or post-filing under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% (plus 2% surtax) for both interest and royalties; under most OECD-style DTAs, the rate is reduced to 10% for interest and royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and meets the limitation-on-benefits clause.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 for cross-border related-party transactions (Local File); Global Master File required for multinational group with consolidated revenue exceeding KRW 100,000,000,000; CbCR when group revenue exceeds KRW 1,000,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a 'substance over form' doctrine and GAAR under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the International Tax Adjustment Act. Non-resident structures must demonstrate genuine business purpose and economic substance; artificial arrangements will be re-characterized and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of revenue, fabrication of expenses, or unlawful evasion of the corporate tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to 3 times the amount of evaded tax, plus additional tax of up to 20% of the unpaid amount and daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in evasion can be personally criminally liable, subjected to civil restitution, and have exit/travel bans imposed by the court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a fictitious Korean entity with no real economic activity, staff, or assets, used merely as a pass-through for profits or to claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under GAAR, NTS may disregard the entity/transaction, deny treaty relief, retroactively reassess tax, add surcharges and interest, and impose penalty tax of up to 40% of the avoided tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced; directors can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, and may face criminal prosecution for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report suspicious transactions involving high-risk payment rails (e.g., anonymous crypto or third-party transfers) or structuring funds to evade the Specified Financial Information Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to KRW 50 million or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both; corporate entities subject to penalty payment orders and possible revocation of licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under AML law for failure to implement KYC/STR procedures; potential imprisonment, travel bans, and forfeiture of proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length prices with related foreign entities without documented TP policy, thereby shifting taxable income from Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS adjustment to arm's length, additional corporate tax on the imputed income, 10% underreporting penalty, 0.022% daily interest, and penalty for failure to produce contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In cases of gross neglect or intent, directors may be held personally liable for penalties and interest; serious violations may trigger criminal prosecution.
